Subject: Post-demo: Performance SLO checklist & MAP items (FinTechCo)

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the deep-dive with the infra and payments teams. Per our call, attaching a concise SLO checklist + MAP (mutual action plan) items so we can hit the evaluation cadence you outlined. Attachment: Redwood_SLO_Checklist_v1.pdf. Demo recording link attached as well.

High-level SLO topics we captured:
- Latency targets (tail objectives): P50 <= 120ms, P95 <= 450ms for 1k token sessions; tail P99 target TBD but would like < 1s where possible.
- Throughput / sustained rate: baseline 200 requests/sec (text-gen single-turn), burst to 400 rps during peak windows.
- Concurrency: expected 50 concurrent sessions for live chat; up to 200 concurrent streaming sessions for realtime product flows.
- Streaming requirements: server-side chunked streaming (SSE/HTTP2) with token-level flush; max acceptable tokenization latency 50ms per chunk.
- Availability/Failover: multi-region fallback and model variant fallback acceptable; need charted RTO/RPO for Dedicated offering.

Proposed MAP next steps:
1) You to confirm decision criteria (latency, throughput, cost target) — noted as action for Alex.
2) Redwood to run a 48-hour soak test against your sample workload (we'll need a representative prompt set + traffic profile).
3) Joint benchmark session with our infra team (Aditya) and your SREs to validate concurrency and streaming behavior.
4) Procurement kickoff once performance gates are met.

Can you confirm the decision criteria and share a sample traffic profile and representative prompts by EOD Monday? I’ll loop in Aditya and Neha to plan the soak and benchmark.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the detailed recap and checklist. Quick clarifications from our side so we can finalize decision criteria: 

1) Latency: Our primary UX KPI is token-to-token latency on streaming sessions. For chat (avg ~150 tokens), we need median token latency < 40ms and 95th < 200ms. For single-turn batch gen (up to 1k tokens) we can accept P95 up to 450ms as you noted.
2) Throughput: 200 rps baseline is right; important that 200 rps is sustained with 95th latency targets met. Peak bursts may be up to 500 rps for short windows (1-5 minutes).
3) Concurrency: 200 concurrent streaming sessions is critical, but note not all sessions will be high-token-rate; about 20% will be heavy (continuous streaming).
4) Fallback: if model variant fallback causes >2x latency increase we may consider that a failed gate.

We’ll share a traffic profile and sample prompt set by Monday EOD. Also forwarding to procurement separately for paperwork.

—Alex
Alex Johnson, Head of ML Platforms | FinTechCo
